candidates.exact_span: This permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that approved State standards in accordance with 40 CFR 122.44(d).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether effluent limitations for some parameters are presently established in the permit versus only potentially forthcoming on reopening affects which enforceable numeric limits are applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: language has been added stating that the permit may be reopened and modified during the life of the permit if relevant portions of the State WQS are revised or remanded.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If WQS revisions can reopen and modify the permit during its term, the operative limits and monitoring requirements for FY2025 may differ depending on whether any revision-triggered modification is treated as already effective or still prospective.

candidates.exact_span: The permit may be reopened to include conditions of the completed TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: TMDL-related conditions may add or alter effluent limitations and associated monitoring; interpretation of whether such conditions are already incorporated or only potential affects which limits and monitoring obligations are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Therefore, no additional requirements beyond the previously described technology-based or water quality-based effluent limitations and monitoring requirements, are established in the proposed permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This caps the set of operative numeric limits and monitoring requirements to those described elsewhere; different readings of what counts as 'previously described' change which limits are enforceable and which monitoring obligations are in scope.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed permit are developed from the State water quality standards and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties both effluent limits and monitoring requirements to WQS-derived basis; interpretation affects which parameters are subject to numeric compliance comparison versus report-only monitoring framed as protective of designated uses.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent discharges flows are intermittent and are not directly discharged to Animas River.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent discharge and indirect routing can change when limits apply, whether monitoring is required only upon discharge occurrence, and how missing or no-result periods are classified as no-discharge versus unresolved evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Facility flows described in the 2016 Statement of Basis were 0.181 MGD and have not increased (now 0.177 MGD as discussed above).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Stated flow magnitude and the assertion that flows have not increased may affect applicability of flow-dependent or dilution-based effluent limits and whether antibacksliding or alteration justifications apply.

candidates.exact_span: The permit requirements and the limits, including mercury, are protective of the receiving waters designated uses of that water consistent with 2020 Water Quality Management Plan and Continuing Planning Process
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicit mention of mercury among operative limits signals mercury as a parameter in scope for numeric limit applicability and likely associated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Antibacksliding stringency rule governs whether a proposed limit can be less stringent than the prior permit; interpretation of whether qualifying alterations occurred changes which numeric limit is applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit maintains the permit requirements of the previous permit for TSS, TRC and pH.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies TSS, TRC, and pH as parameters whose prior-permit limits and requirements are carried forward; interpretation affects which enforceable limits and monitoring obligations apply for those parameters in FY2025.
